title: Get the CRUE: A simple Guide to Surf Portuguese Bureaucracy
author: Atlean World
excerpt: So, you're embracing life in Portugal and eyeing that CRUE document for healthcare bliss and an NIF to keep your tax matters in check. Let's break it down in the friendliest way possible.
body:
So, you're embracing life in Portugal and eyeing that CRUE document for healthcare bliss and
an NIF to keep your tax matters in check. Let's break it down in the friendliest way possible.

What's the CRUE Document, anyway?

The CRUE (Certificado de Registo de Utente) is your golden ticket to Portugal's residency as well as unlocking the possibility to live the country at its fullest like enjoying employment contracts, healthcare and social security, among other benefits.

Now, let's get you started on the journey to snagging this essential piece of paperwork.
Before even starting the CRUE process, there are 3 documents that we need to check first:

● Proof of Residence
● NISS (Number of Social Security)
● NIF (Tax Number)

Step 1: Gather Your Documents

First things first, let's round up the following paperwork:

Proof of Residency: This can be a rental contract or a utility bill in your name. Basically,
something that says, "Hey, I live here!"

If you're living with friends, a signed letter from the homeowner stating that you reside there is your golden ticket. Include a copy of their ID or passport to sweeten the deal.
To be easier, you can go to your local “Junta de Freguesia” with the homeowner, and have a declaration signed that will prove your residency.

Check your local parish council where you are living.

ID or Passport: Your ID or passport is your identity proof – crucial for making things official.

Step 2: The Local Health Center and the Mighty NISS

Head to your local health center or "centro de saúde'' to kickstart the process. But wait, there's a superhero in this story: the NISS (Número de Identificação da Segurança Social). It's your social security number, a must for the CRUE journey.

At the health center, make a beeline for the registration desk. Politely explain you're on a mission to get your CRUE document and NISS. They'll guide you through the next steps.

Expect some paperwork – nothing too intimidating. Fill out forms with your personal info and details from the docs you brought along. It's like a healthcare membership, but better.
Hand over your forms and documents. They'll verify everything, and there might be a bit of a wait. Keep that book or podcast handy – it'll make the time fly.

Drumroll, please!

Once everything checks out, you'll be handed your NISS. It's official – Portugal welcomes you into its healthcare and social security embrace.

Step 3: The NIF – Your Tax Mate

Ah, the NIF (Número de Identificação Fiscal), your tax companion. Head to the local Finanças office or the Tax Authority. Fill out a form, bring your ID or passport, and there you go – you're officially tax-ready in Portugal. (this process may be done on the first visit)

Step 4: Get the CRUE

⚠️Do you know that “Cru”means “raw”, so everytime you are explaining this process to a Portuguese they are most likely imagining their raw food and probably not fully hearing you... just warning

Now that you have the required documentation, it is time to visit the Municipality where you are living.

If you are not sure where to go, feel free to check on this national website what is the exact place to go: https://anmp.pt/en/municipios/municipios/municipios-de-a-a-v/

While visiting the municipality, you can request the CRUE. They will collect the documentation and initiate the process. This process usually takes around 2 weeks and has a cost fee. You can check the full details on their official website: https://www.servicopublico.pt/crue-certificado-do-registo-de-cidadao-da-ue/

Final Words of Wisdom

Patience is Your Superpower: The process might take a bit, so breathe and be patient. Your friendly attitude goes a long way.

Check and Recheck: Before your trip, make sure your documents are in order. It's a sanity-saving move.

Ask Away: If you're confused, ask questions. The health center and Finanças folks as well as the people in the Municipality are there to help you navigate the process.

There you have it – a simple, friendly guide to CRUE. With your paperwork sorted, you're not just in Portugal; you're officially part of the Portuguese system.

Make it happen and ENJOY!

title: Why is it crucial to have experience with customers?
author: Atlean World
excerpt: Customer relations should never be underestimated. It is now at the heart of corporate strategies, as it addresses many issues and contributes fully to business development by increasing sales and building customer loyalty, among other things.
body:
Customer relations should never be underestimated. It is now at the heart of corporate strategies, as it addresses many issues and contributes fully to business development by increasing sales and building customer loyalty, among other things.

Although the work can be difficult, the rewards are unequaled. Not only does working in customer service mean that you are the face of the company, which is an interesting responsibility in itself, but it also allows you to make a real contribution to improving people's lives.

1.You will improve and develop several skills

When you work in customer service, you often have to wear several hats at the same time. In your daily work you have to be operational and know how to use several different skills.

In addition, it also allows you to acquire new skills that will be very useful in your future career, such as: attention, patience, communication, organization, multitasking and others.

2.You will be an expert in problem solving

It is obvious that problem solving (more or less technical) is the bread and butter of the job. Whether we are talking about a quick fix or a multi-step process, in order to solve each case you will need to apply your human skills, creative thinking and expertise.

This problem-solving ability (fast, diplomatically and efficiently) is crucial in any job, whether it is in customer service or not. It is the lifeblood of prioritization, project management and conflict resolution. All these skills are necessary to manage a team, achieve your goals or simply get promoted.

3. Many possibilities for progression

Once you have entered the customer service environment, there are many opportunities for growth. If you think that there are no opportunities for development in customer service, you are very much mistaken. If there is one thing that all companies have in common, it is satisfying their customers and building loyalty. This sector is characterized by a wide variety of jobs, including:

  • the customer relations manager, who defines and implements the strategy and monitors its results using performance indicators
  • the team manager, who manages a team in order to achieve the objectives set
  • the quality manager, who proposes action plans to improve the quality of services
  • the community manager, whose objective is to animate and unite a community on social networks
  • the telemarketer, who is none other than a salesperson who works remotely, not in the field
  • the training manager, who determines a training policy to develop the skills of employees 

4. Free training courses

The vast majority of companies that recruit customer service offer free training to all their employees. Whether it's initial or ongoing training, it will allow you to add more strings to your bow.

There are also many companies that invest in the development of their employees by offering more specific training (such as marketing, management, sales, training, etc.), which will not cost the employee anything. This is a very good option to further develop your communication skills or other skills.

Moreover, you can also train on the use of specific software that will be beneficial for your future (such as Amadeus, Zendesk, among others).

5. Bonuses in addition to salary

Depending on the type of project and position, working in customer service you can also get very interesting monthly and annual bonuses. If it is a more sales-oriented position, the bonuses will of course be higher. However, many customer services that do not require sales also offer bonuses based on customer satisfaction and other KPIs.

6. Mastering different communication channels

Nowadays, customer service is not just about the phone, but rather about using different support channels. You will therefore be working with your customers by phone in the morning, by email in the afternoon or even by chat for simple questions. With this, you will eventually master the art of numeric communication.

Here are different support channels:

  • Email
  • Phone
  • Social networks
  • Forums
  • Chat
  • SMS

Knowing how to communicate effectively on these various platforms will allow you to build relationships with people of various backgrounds and ages, who you haven't met in person. A very useful skill!

7. Working with a multicultural team

It can't be said enough, working in a multicultural environment has only benefits.

Customer support teams are not all of the same nationality, cultural background and are made up of different personalities with unique perspectives. Every day you will learn something new about your colleagues when you work on a project together.

Being exposed to a range of different perspectives is very useful in your career development. You may find solutions to problems you never knew existed, or change your mind about an issue after looking at it from another angle.

Not to mention the fact that working with people who come from another country than your own will allow you to discover new things about their culture, customs or habits. This will make you more open-minded and strengthen your general culture.

8. Build your own network

You don't always think about it, but when you work in customer support you can quickly build up your own network of contacts.

You may not always have the answer to a customer's question or you may have to share customer feedback with important stakeholders. To achieve all this you will have to draw on the knowledge of your colleagues. In doing so, you will create a network of colleagues with different skills from your own and thus create a network of new opportunities for professional growth and development.

Whether you aspire to a long-term career in customer support or are simply interested in getting your foot in the door of an emerging company, a job in customer support will provide you with valuable skills that you will always need in your career.

title: 5 reasons to have an overseas experience
author: Atlean World
excerpt: Leave everything behind and go live abroad! Although the idea may seem frightening, it is without a doubt one of the best decisions to make. Today we are going to see why going to live abroad has multiple advantages.
body:
Leave everything behind and go live abroad!

Although the idea may seem frightening, it is without a doubt one of the best decisions to make. Today we are going to see why going to live abroad has multiple advantages.

Whether you choose a country close to your own or on the other side of the world, living an experience abroad represents a real added value to your career.

In this article, we give you 5 good reasons why you should be able to check the box "experience abroad" before starting your career.

Also worth reading: ADAPTING ABROAD: A GUIDE TO OVERCOMING CHALLENGES

1. Discover a different culture and have a truly unique adventure

Once you've lived abroad, you'll come back changed!

It is a unique and intense experience. Each country has its own culture, its own customs and landscapes. By immersing yourself in a foreign country, you will discover all its facets (customs, culture, politics, populations, gastronomy etc.) which are sometimes quite different from those you know.

Moreover, these cultural differences allow you to look at your own culture in a different way. No more prejudices and hello open-mindedness! You can thus discover a new way of life while working.

2. Build self-confidence and self-reliance 

Experiencing life abroad strengthens your ability to adapt to a new and sometimes complex environment. It is an excellent way to get out of your comfort zone, but also to develop your human qualities, such as tolerance and open-mindedness.

When you arrive in a foreign country, you will have to fend for yourself. This will allow you to gain maturity and autonomy. Without your family and friends, you will be forced to manage on your own. It is a wonderful experience to gain confidence in yourself and to realize what you are capable of.

Not only is the belief that you can thrive anywhere a boon to your self-esteem, but it speaks volumes to future employers about the type of person you are and what you are capable of. This unique ability to show real-life examples of struggles you've overcome is an advantage not everyone has.

3. Become fluent in a language / learn a new language

Whether it is from a personal or professional point of view, learning a new language will not only strengthen your resume but also you as a human being. We've told you often enough, immersion is the best way to become fluent in a language because it allows you to master it in its smallest details by practicing it every day. This can be during dinners, evenings, in your daily work...

One tip? Don't be afraid and go for it! The more you practice the less mistakes you will make

Being bilingual is a great asset. In today's world, mastering a second language has become almost indispensable.

4. Enhance your CV

Do you want your profile to stand out from the many CVs received by companies? Experience abroad has its weight.

To enhance your profile, it is essential to be able to demonstrate that you have good adaptation skills, as well as an open mind and intellectual curiosity. And for that, there is nothing better than an experience abroad! On your CV, an experience abroad is more and more appreciated by professionals. It shows a certain dynamism on your part as well as your ability to adapt.

A little extra: In today's globalized world, a profile that mentions a life experience abroad will be more appreciated by multinational firms.

5. Expand your network

You may find yourself alone at first, but making new contacts is a major benefit of living abroad. Having friends with different backgrounds and life experiences will also enrich your cultural knowledge. Meeting people with different life experiences from your own will be an interesting way to spend your time. It will also help you integrate into your new country.

It is also a great way to build and grow your address book. A good international network of connections will certainly help you in your professional development. You never know, you might meet people who work in the same field as you and offer you wonderful job opportunities!

title: You are looking for a job: 4 signs that you are dealing with a reliable recruitment agency
author: Atlean World
excerpt: The recruitment process is a long process and looking for a job can be a full-time job in itself.
body:
The recruitment process is a long process and looking for a job can be a full-time job in itself.  It means spending a lot of time on applications that may get you nowhere, or a working environment that does not suit you.

This is why a recruitment agency can be useful. Also known as a placement agency, these organizations focus on jobs and companies that are right for you and save you a lot of time in your search for the perfect job.

It acts as an intermediary between a potential employer and qualified candidates who have the background and skills the employer is looking for.

It works in partnership with employers who are looking to fill vacancies.

1 - A good recruitment agency will save the candidate a lot of time

The goal is to speed up the hiring process so that the experience is more positive and has more impact on both sides.

The recruiter already knows the market and the various profiles requested by companies. He will be able to adapt your profile to the one required by the client (the hiring company) and he can also prepare you for job interviews.

An agency is in constant contact with the employer's recruitment manager and often has information about the recruitment process. This information may include: specific qualities the employer is looking for in a candidate, employer's salary range, the personality of the hiring manager, among others.

For these reasons, an agency may send you to the interview with a definite advantage over the competition.

2 – A good recruitment agency will put candidates and clients at the center of their operations.

The human element, communication or the importance of long-term relationships with both candidates and clients, are among the main features of a solid and reliable placement agency.

This means that the relationship does not end once the position is filled: there is always a close follow up to see if everything is going well for both parties.

It also means, for example, that the recruiter stays in touch with candidates throughout their careers, which can be useful in finding talented people who are not actively looking for work.

It is also important to know that even if the recruiter tries to find the ideal job for all his candidates, the result is not always successful.

Fortunately, the job market is always in flux, and when one door closes, another can open very quickly. The consultant has many opportunities to work with his candidates again and continue to do so until the right professional opportunity is found.

3. A good recruitment agency will communicate with transparency

A good placement agency takes pride in not only building, but also maintaining strong relationships with the candidates.

Having this trust allows one to know the ideal candidates that are desired for a particular job by companies and the recruiter uses his time to prepare candidates to make the best use of skills and assets and to guide them into the next stage of their career.

Throughout the process, he will have full transparency with the candidates to ensure that everything is clear, that everything runs smoothly and that there are no nasty surprises.

The recruiter is faced with the job market every day: he listens to both employers and candidates, which gives him a strong knowledge of the sector.

It is necessary to explain to candidates the steps that will follow their contact with the agency and what they can expect from it.  It is essential to give truthful and honest advice.

Listening is to understand. A recruiter needs to listen and pay attention to the people he is talking to. In order to work efficiently and qualitatively, he needs to know exactly what he is looking for and what he can offer. He must be curious, proactive and available!

By taking into account feedback from companies and candidates, a solid placement agency can only improve and excel.

4 - Have the agency's recruiters actually worked in the field?

Working with a recruitment company whose staff have actually worked in your sector is essential if you are to find the ideal job. Every profession has its nuances and complexities and recruiters who have been industry insiders are uniquely placed to address the unique challenges associated with the sector they serve.

A good recruitment agency is first and foremost one that has experience in your field of activity. It will be better able to understand the issues and to identify the profiles of the candidates.

It is in a recruiter's interest to keep abreast of sector-specific salaries and market trends. Whether it's information about the local market or the international market for a specialty, you can always rely on your recruiter to point you in the right direction and give you relevant advice.

In summary, the recruitment industry is more about creating relationships, creating opportunities.

Although recruitment is fundamentally about 'getting people to work', it is really about connecting people with companies.

title: Exploring the Wonders of Lisbon
author: Atlean World
excerpt: A typical question in a job interview: "What are your strengths and weaknesses?" How to answer without sounding cliché?
body:
Lisbon, Portugal, is a city that effortlessly blends the charm of its past with the vibrancy of the present. As you wander through its cobblestone streets and climb its hills, you'll uncover a city that's steeped in history and alive with energy.

Here is what you can expect if you decide to move to Lisbon:

Historical Gems

Lisbon's old neighborhoods, like Alfama and Baixa, are like a journey back in time. Twisty streets, colorful buildings, and ancient landmarks tell stories of days gone by. The São Jorge Castle, perched on a hill, gives you a panoramic view of the city, while the Jerónimos Monastery showcases beautiful old architecture.

Art and Creativity

Art lovers will find joy in Lisbon's museums. The Museu Nacional de Arte Antiga holds a bunch of cool Portuguese art, and the Berardo Collection Museum is like a modern art wonderland. Walk around the city, and you'll see walls painted with bright, beautiful murals.

Tasty Adventures

Lisbon's food scene is a treat for your taste buds. Fresh seafood, yummy custard tarts called pastel de nata, and a food market turned Time Out Market offer a feast of flavors from Portugal.

Also worth reading: Moving to Portugal - 5 reasons to settle here

Fado Music

You can't visit Lisbon without feeling the soulful tunes of Fado. In the historic neighborhood of Alfama, tiny Fado houses bring the music to life, telling emotional stories through songs.

Mix of Old and New

Lisbon isn't just about history; it's a city that's moving forward. Cool neighborhoods like Chiado and Bairro Alto have trendy shops, art spaces, and a nightlife that buzzes with excitement. The LX Factory, once an industrial area, is now a creative space, showing off Lisbon's modern side.

Nature Escapes

If you need a break from the city, Lisbon has you covered. Take a short trip to Sintra to see fairy-tale palaces and gardens, or hop on a train to Cascais for a peaceful day at the beach.

In every street and every corner, Lisbon welcomes you with warmth, offering a mix of old and new that's simply enchanting. Whether you're into the history of Alfama or the cool vibes of Bairro Alto, Lisbon is ready to show you its magic.

title: The Dance of Balance - Weaving Work and Life in Harmony
author: Atlean World
excerpt: A typical question in a job interview: "What are your strengths and weaknesses?" How to answer without sounding cliché?
body:
In the fast-paced rhythm of modern life, finding the right balance between our professional commitments and personal well-being has become more crucial than ever. The concept of work-life balance is not merely a catchphrase but a cornerstone for leading a fulfilling and sustainable life.

Let's understand the importance of striking this balance and the positive impact it can have on both our professional and personal lives.

Enhanced Productivity

A well-balanced life contributes to increased productivity in the workplace. When we prioritize time for relaxation, family, and personal interests, we return to work with an empty mind and a greater capacity to focus. This not only enhances our ability to face challenges but also fosters a creative and innovative mindset, bringing fresh perspectives to our professional spheres.

Health and Well-Being

Maintaining a healthy work-life balance is closely linked to overall well-being. Long hours at work, without adequate time for rest, can lead to a burnout and a decline in physical and mental health.

On the other hand, a balanced approach that includes regular breaks, exercise, and quality time spent with loved ones contributes to better health, reduced stress, and increased resilience to face life's challenges.

Strengthened Relationships

Balancing work commitments with personal life nurtures stronger relationships. Quality time invested in family, friends, and social activities contributes to a sense of connection and support. This, in turn, leads to a positive mindset, creating a foundation of emotional well-being that spills over into our professional life, promoting collaboration and teamwork.

Professional Satisfaction

Achieving a work-life balance is integral to experiencing satisfaction and fulfillment. It allows us to set realistic goals, manage work-related stress, and appreciate the value of our contributions.

A workforce that feels happy and satisfied tends to be more engaged, loyal, and committed, positively impacting both individual and organizational success.

Continuous Learning and Growth

A well-rounded life encourages continuous learning and personal growth. Engaging in activities beyond the workplace, such as pursuing hobbies, attending classes, or spending time in self-reflection, contributes to a holistic development.

Experiences like these bring new perspectives and skills, enhancing our adaptability and resilience in the face of change.

Setting Boundaries

Establishing clear boundaries between work and personal life is a fundamental aspect of achieving balance. This involves defining specific working hours, resisting the urge to constantly check work emails outside of those hours, and taking planned breaks.

By creating a structured routine, individuals can manage their time effectively, ensuring that work does not encroach upon the precious moments dedicated to personal matters.

Long-Term Sustainability

A balanced approach to work and life is not just about the present; it's an investment in long-term sustainability.

Avoiding burnouts and chronic stress preserves our physical and mental health, allowing us to maintain a steady pace over the course of our careers. This approach not only benefits individuals but also contributes to a more resilient and sustainable workforce as a whole.

In conclusion, work-life balance is not a luxury but a necessity for a healthy, satisfying, and sustainable life. It is a dynamic equilibrium that requires conscious effort and prioritization. By recognizing the importance of nurturing both our professional and personal aspects, we lay the foundation for a fulfilling and harmonious life journey.

Striking this balance is not a one-time achievement but an ongoing process that contributes to our well-being and success in the ever-evolving landscape of work and life.

title: The Transformative Essence of Travel - A journey without boundaries
author: Atlean World
excerpt: A typical question in a job interview: "What are your strengths and weaknesses?" How to answer without sounding cliché?
body:
In human existence, travel emerges as a vibrant thread, weaving together cultures, histories, and personal narratives. Beyond the logistical act of moving from one place to another, the importance of global exploration encompasses a profound impact on our understanding of the world and ourselves.

Traveling is important not only for our minds but also for our souls, so let us delve into the significance of embarking on a journey beyond borders.

Here are some of the reasons that turn traveling into a fundamental piece in our lives:

Cultural Enrichment

One of the paramount reasons to travel the world lies in the opportunity for cultural enrichment.

Traveling offers an immersion into diverse cultures, allowing travelers to witness and appreciate the richness of human expression across different societies. Being in touch with local cuisines, attending traditional ceremonies, and engaging with the arts is what gives an appreciation for the varied ways people experience and express life.

Expanded Perspectives

Beyond the confines of routine, travel acts as a catalyst for expanding perspectives.

Stepping into unfamiliar territories challenges preconceived notions and fosters a more nuanced understanding of the world. Whether it's witnessing historical monuments or navigating through daily lives in a foreign city, these experiences contribute to a comprehensive worldview, instilling empathy and a sense of interconnectedness.

Educational Odyssey

Travel is a form of education that transcends classroom boundaries.

Standing in front of history, exploring museums, and delving into the architectural wonders of different civilizations provide a connection to the lessons of the past. The educational value of travel is not only in gaining knowledge but in getting insights that resonate on a personal level.

Personal Growth and Self-Discovery

Embarking on a journey beyond familiar landscapes is, fundamentally, a journey into oneself.

The challenges and opportunities presented by new environments nurture personal growth and self-discovery. The ability to adapt to unfamiliar circumstances, make decisions in unknown territories, and engage with diverse perspectives contributes to the development of resilience, adaptability, and a deeper understanding of one's own strengths and limitations.

Building Global Connections

Travel serves as a bridge between people, transcending geographical and cultural boundaries.

Interactions with individuals from different backgrounds provide a platform for the exchange of ideas. Friendships made during travels often endure beyond the duration of the trip, creating a network of connections that enrich our lives with many perspectives and shared experiences.

Adaptability

Exposure to different environments and ways of life enhances adaptability - the ability to adapt to new and unexpected situations.

Getting to know a foreign culture, learning to communicate in a different language, and understanding alternative social norms contribute to mental agility. This flexibility and adaptability become an invaluable assets in an interconnected and rapidly evolving world.

Well-Being and Reflection

Travel, in its essence, is a respite for the soul. Stepping away from the familiar rhythm of daily life provides an opportunity for reflection and rejuvenation.

Whether it's the serenity of a natural landscape or the vibrant energy of a bustling city, different environments offer a unique space for introspection, relaxation, and the renewal of mental and emotional well-being.

In conclusion, the importance of traveling extends far beyond the surface of a passport or the thrill of discovering new landscapes. It is a transformative journey that enriches our understanding of cultures, fosters personal growth, and connects us to a broader tapestry of humanity. Each step taken beyond borders adds experience, empathy, and wisdom.

title: Adapting Abroad: A Guide to Overcoming Challenges
author: João Penouço
excerpt: A typical question in a job interview: "What are your strengths and weaknesses?" How to answer without sounding cliché?
body:
Moving abroad is an exciting adventure that can bring about a world of opportunities. Whether it's for work, studies, or a change of scenery, living in a new country can be an enriching experience. However, adapting to life in a foreign land can be a challenging task. At Atlean World, we understand that relocating to a new country can be both thrilling and daunting. In this guide, we'll explore some key aspects of adapting when moving abroad, including learning the local language, getting to know the place and its people, and dealing with homesickness.

Finding Accommodation:

Locating a comfortable and safe place to live is essential for a successful transition to a new country. Here's how to navigate the challenges of finding accommodation:

  • Research and Planning: Begin your search well in advance. Explore different neighborhoods, housing options, and rental prices in your new city. Utilize online resources, such as real estate websites and local forums, to gather information.
  • Budget Considerations: Determine your budget for housing. Be sure to include not only the rent but also utilities, maintenance costs, and any required deposits. It's crucial to find a balance between affordability and quality.
  • Local Rental Market: Understand the local rental market dynamics. In some cities, finding suitable accommodation can be highly competitive, while in others, you might have more options to choose from. Be prepared for various scenarios.
  • Local Customs and Leases: Be aware of local customs regarding renting and lease agreements. Rental terms, security deposits, and notice periods can vary widely from country to country. Seek legal advice if needed to ensure you understand your rights and obligations as a tenant.
  • Viewing Properties: If possible, visit properties in person or take a virtual tour to inspect them thoroughly. Look for issues like safety, cleanliness, and accessibility to public transport, schools, and other essential amenities.
  • Language Barrier: Overcoming the language barrier when dealing with landlords or property agents can be challenging. If you're not proficient in the local language, consider seeking help from a local friend or hiring a translator to ensure clear communication.
  • Temporary Housing: If you can't secure a permanent residence before your move, consider temporary housing options like hotels, hostels, or serviced apartments. This provides you with a place to stay while you continue your search.
  • Negotiation Skills: Hone your negotiation skills when discussing rental terms and prices. Understanding local customs and market conditions can help you secure a more favorable deal.

Pro tip: When making friends, ask them to share the contact of their landlord so you can reach them directly. If they can’t help you, maybe they will know someone that can.

Also worth reading: Accommodation in Greece: How to find a place to live

Learning the Local Language:

One of the biggest challenges when moving abroad is the language barrier. Learning the local language is a crucial step in adapting to your new environment. Here are some tips to make the process smoother:

  • Language Classes: Enroll in language classes, either online or in-person, to build your language skills. Many countries offer free or affordable language courses for newcomers.
  • Language Apps: Utilize language-learning apps such as Duolingo, Babbel, or Rosetta Stone to practice daily. Consistency is key to improving your language skills.
  • Practice with Locals: Interact with native speakers. Don't be shy to make mistakes, as it's a part of the learning process. The locals will appreciate your efforts to speak their language.
  • Immerse Yourself: Watch local TV shows, read newspapers, and listen to radio broadcasts in the local language. This will help you understand the culture and colloquial expressions better.

Getting to Know the Place and Its People:

Exploring your new surroundings is an essential part of adapting to life abroad. Here are some tips to help you settle in and feel at home:

  • City Exploration: Start with a city tour. Visit landmarks, museums, and parks to get to know the history and culture of your new home.
  • Local Food Adventures: Trying the local cuisine is a delightful way to connect with the culture. Explore local restaurants and markets to savor the flavors of your new home.
  • Meetup Groups: Join local meetup groups or social clubs related to your interests. This is a great way to meet like-minded people and build friendships.
  • Ask for Recommendations: Don't hesitate to ask colleagues, neighbors, or acquaintances for recommendations on places to visit, dine, or enjoy local entertainment.

Pro tip: book a free tour to have a genuine overview of the city and get to know the most interesting hidden spots or off-road tracks. Don’t forget to tip your tour guide

Also worth reading: Moving to Portugal: 5 reasons to settle there

Dealing with Homesickness:

Homesickness is a common feeling when moving abroad. It's natural to miss your family, friends, and familiar surroundings. Here's how to cope with homesickness:

  • Stay Connected: Keep in touch with loved ones through video calls, messages, or social media. Knowing they are just a call away can provide comfort.
  • Create a Home Away from Home: Personalize your new space with familiar items from your home country. It can be as simple as framed photos or familiar scents.
  • Set Goals: Establish goals for your time abroad, both personal and professional. Achieving these goals can help shift your focus and make you feel more integrated.
  • Find a Support System: Seek out local support groups or expat communities. These networks can provide guidance, friendship, and a sense of belonging.

Navigating Cultural Differences:

Moving to a new country often means encountering a different culture, which can be both fascinating and challenging. Here are some aspects to consider:

  • Cultural Awareness: Take the time to understand the local customs, traditions, and social norms. What might be polite in your home country could be considered rude in your new home. Be open to learning and adapting.
  • Cultural Shock: It's common to experience culture shock when confronted with new ways of life. This can include differences in communication styles, social hierarchies, and work practices. Be patient with yourself as you adjust.
  • Respect and Tolerance: Embrace diversity and practice tolerance. Be respectful of the beliefs and practices of the local culture, even if they differ from your own. Engaging with the culture can lead to a deeper understanding and appreciation of your new home.

Legal and Administrative Challenges:

Dealing with legal and administrative aspects in a foreign country can be a significant challenge. Here's how to navigate these hurdles:

  • Visa and Documentation: Ensure that you have all the necessary visas and permits to live and work in your new country legally. Familiarize yourself with the local immigration rules and regulations to avoid any legal issues.
  • Banking and Finances: Opening a bank account, understanding local taxes, and managing your finances can be complex. Seek assistance from professionals or expat-friendly banks to make this process easier.
  • Healthcare and Insurance: Learn about the local healthcare system and secure appropriate health insurance. Familiarize yourself with how to access medical care and emergency services.
  • Local Laws and Regulations: Understand the local laws and regulations. Familiarize yourself with the legal system, including rights and responsibilities. Ignorance of the law is not an excuse in a new country.

Adapting to life in a new country may take time, but with determination and an open mind, it can be an incredibly rewarding experience.

At Atlean World, we are here to support you in your journey to finding your place in your new home.

Moving abroad is an exciting but challenging experience.

Learning the local language, exploring the place, and dealing with homesickness are all part of the process. Keep in mind that adapting takes time, so be patient with yourself.

Embrace the adventure, and you'll find yourself growing and evolving in ways you never imagined. Enjoy the journey, and make the most of this incredible opportunity to broaden your horizons and create lasting memories.

title: Relocate with your pet: The guide to do it
author: João Penouço
excerpt: Our article guides you through the essential steps to ensure a stress-free trip and a smooth transition to your new life abroad with your pet
body:
Moving to a new country in Europe is an exciting adventure, but when you're a pet owner, it adds an extra layer of complexity to the process. The first question that comes to mind is: "How can I relocate with my pet, and what are the steps involved?"

If you have been in the spot you know it can be “complicated”, if it is the first time you are considering this, you can face some struggles.

Good news is, with careful planning and awareness of the rules and regulations, relocating with your furry companion can be a smooth and rewarding experience.

Our article guides you through the essential steps to ensure a stress-free trip and a smooth transition to your new life abroad with your furry companion

Step 1: Pet Passport and Microchipping

One of the first things you'll need to do is ensure your pet has a valid pet passport. A pet passport is a document that allows your pet to travel within the European Union (EU) and some other countries, just like a human passport. To obtain one, your pet must be microchipped for identification, vaccinated against rabies, and receive any necessary boosters. Keep in mind that these requirements may vary from country to country, so it's crucial to check the specific regulations of your destination. All of the EU countries require the Microchipping, but you can check the full list on the following link: pettravel.com/passports_microchip_countries.cfm

Step 2: Health Check and Vaccinations

Before your departure, schedule a visit to the veterinarian for a thorough health check. Your pet's vaccinations should be up-to-date, and your vet can provide you with a certificate of good health, which is often required by airlines and immigration authorities. This certificate usually needs to be issued within a specific timeframe before your travel date. We truly recommend at least 1 month to deal with these steps, to take into consideration the time for the appointment with the veterinarian, the vaccination itself and the potential (natural) reaction your pet may have. Remember, this process should also be smooth for your best friend! Their comfort is our happiness after all, right?

Step 3: Choosing the Right Flights and Airlines

When it comes to flying with your pet, choosing the right airline and flight is crucial.

Not all airlines have the same policies and conditions for pet travel, so do your research and select an airline that prioritizes the safety and comfort of your furry friend.

It's essential to book your flight well in advance and inform the airline that you will be traveling with a pet to secure a spot for your pet in the cabin or cargo hold.

Within Europe you can find several airlines that you can chose to travel with your Pet.

Here are some of the examples of airlines where you can book the spot for your fellow.

Swiss International Airlines

Turkish Airlines

Lufthansa Airlines

Aeroflot

TAP Air Portugal

SAS

KLM

Iberia

Aegean Airways

Step 4: Preparing Your Pet for the Journey

To ensure your pet's comfort during the journey, consider crate training before the trip.

Familiarize your pet with the travel crate to reduce anxiety during the flight. Pack essential items like food, water, toys, and a blanket to make your pet feel at ease. Keep in mind that some countries may require additional documents or quarantine periods upon arrival, so research these requirements in advance.

Step 5: Finding a Pet-Friendly Home

Once you've arrived at your destination, finding a pet-friendly place to live is a top priority.

Research the local housing market and look for rental properties or neighborhoods that are known for being pet-friendly.

It's a good idea to work with a real estate agent who specializes in pet-friendly properties to help you navigate the housing market more effectively.

Advantages of Traveling with a Pet

Traveling with your pet can be immensely rewarding. Here are some of the advantages:

  • Companionship: Pets provide emotional support and companionship during the stressful period of relocation. They can help reduce anxiety and make the transition smoother.
  • Exercise and Exploration: Having a pet encourages you to explore your new surroundings. Daily walks with your dog or outdoor adventures with your cat can help you discover your new city.
  • Routine and Stability: Pets thrive on routines, which can help establish a sense of stability in your life as you settle into a new environment.

Impact on Work-Life Balance

Pets can positively impact your work-life balance. They remind you to take breaks and enjoy the outdoors, reducing work-related stress. Additionally, having a pet waiting for you at home can make your work-life balance feel more fulfilling and enjoyable.

Conclusion

When you move abroad, relocate with your pet requires careful planning and adherence to regulations, but the joy and companionship your pet brings are well worth the effort. With a pet passport, the right flights, proper preparations, and a pet-friendly home, your journey can be a memorable and enjoyable experience for both you and your furry friend. Embrace the adventure, and let your pet be your steadfast companion as you explore your new European home.

title: Accommodation in Greece: How to find a place to live
author: João Penouço
excerpt: Discover your corner of paradise in Greece! Our article reveals the secrets to finding your accommodation in this Mediterranean gem.
body:
Greece, with its breathtaking natural beauty, rich historical heritage and delicious cuisine, has long been a dream destination for many people from all over the world. Whether for an unforgettable vacation, relocation or property investment, Greece offers a multitude of exciting opportunities. However, in the vast Greek real estate landscape, finding the perfect accommodation can sometimes seem like a complex quest.

In this guide, we'll walk you through the steps to help you secure a place to call home in this beautiful country.

Documentation Needed

The search for your ideal apartment in Greece begins with meticulous preparation, and this involves gathering the essential documents to ensure that your search goes smoothly. Buying or renting property in Greece can be a rewarding experience, but it's also a process that requires meticulous attention to administrative details.

In this first part of our guide, we'll walk you through the key documents you'll need to prepare and understand in order to facilitate your property search in Greece. Whether you're an international investor or a future Greek resident, this list of essential documents is your starting point for a successful search.

If you are from a country that will require a Visa, then additional steps may apply first in how to get this documentation. We recommend in this case contacting the Greek embassy in the country you are from to get better informed.

If you are from a country in the EU, you won't need to worry about visa sponsorship or embassy work, you can jump to the next steps.

You will need the following documents

  • Valid Identification

Ensure you have a valid passport or ID card, as it will be required for various administrative processes.

  • Tax Identification Number (AFM)

To rent property in Greece, you'll need an AFM (Αριθμός Φορολογικού Μητρώου). This number is essential for any financial transactions, including signing a lease agreement.

Searching for Accommodation

Now that you have your documentation in order, let's explore how to find the perfect accommodation in Greece. Local real estate websites, real estate agencies and social networking groups specializing in real estate are excellent resources to start your search. In addition, don't hesitate to seek advice from expats or locals, as their valuable information can help you better understand the Greek real estate market and make informed decisions.

Real Estate Agencies

Real estate agencies play a significant role in the Greek property market. They have extensive listings, can assist with negotiations, and offer valuable insights into local housing trends.

Consider contacting reputable agencies in your desired area to discuss your preferences and budget.

Online Websites

The internet has made house hunting more accessible than ever. Websites like Idealista, Spitogatos, and Kyero, Spiti24 offer a vast selection of properties across Greece. You can filter listings by location, size, and price range, making it easier to find options that match your needs.

Accommodation Options and Price Range

Now, let's explore the price range for different types of accommodation options in Greece. Keep in mind that prices may vary depending on the city and neighborhood. It's essential to define your criteria and preferences. The range of accommodation on offer in Greece is varied, from city-center apartments to picturesque country houses and seaside villas. Before plunging into your search, take time to think about your budget, desired location, size of accommodation and necessary amenities. Once you have a clear idea of what you're looking for, you can explore the various options available.

  • Studios: Studios are a popular choice for individuals or couples looking for budget-friendly options. In Greece, you can find studios ranging from €200 to €500 per month. The price will depend on factors like location and amenities.
  • One-Room Apartments: One-room apartments offer more space and privacy. Prices for one-room apartments typically start at €300 and can go up to €600 per month. Again, location plays a significant role in determining the cost.
  • Two-Room Apartments: If you need extra space or plan to share with a roommate, two-room apartments are a great choice. These can range from €400 to €1,000 per month, depending on size, location, and amenities.

Tips for a Smooth Transition

For a smooth transition when looking for accommodation in Greece, it's essential to take a few preparatory steps. Here are a few tips to help you make the transition.

  • Local Knowledge: Take advantage of local knowledge. Talk to locals, expats, or online forums to gain insights into the best neighborhoods, rental prices, and any potential challenges.
  • Visit Properties: Whenever possible, visit the properties in person. Photos can be deceiving, and seeing the place firsthand will help you make an informed decision.
  • Negotiate: Don't hesitate to negotiate the rent. In Greece, there's often room for negotiation, especially if you're signing a long-term lease.
  • Legal Assistance: Consider hiring a local lawyer or real estate agent to assist with legal aspects, such as reviewing lease agreements and ensuring a smooth rental process.

Conclusion

Finding accommodation in Greece can be an exciting journey, offering you the opportunity to immerse yourself in the country's vibrant culture and natural beauty. With the right documentation, a well-planned search, and a clear budget in mind, you'll be well on your way to discovering your ideal home in Greece. Whether you're drawn to the bustling streets of Athens, the serene islands, or the historic towns, Greece has a wide range of housing options to suit every lifestyle and budget. Embrace the adventure, and soon enough, you'll be enjoying the Mediterranean lifestyle in your new Greek home.

title: How to Get an AFM in Greece: Your Key to Mediterranean Life
author: João Penouço
excerpt: If you're planning to live, work, or invest in Greece, there's a crucial document you'll need to obtain the AFM, also known as the Tax Identification Number.
body:
If you're planning to live, work, or invest in Greece, there's a crucial document you'll need to obtain—the AFM (Αριθμός Φορολογικού Μητρώου), also known as the Tax Identification Number.

This unique number is your ticket to navigating the Greek bureaucracy and conducting various financial transactions. In this guide, we'll walk you through the process of obtaining an AFM, including the documentation needed, the steps to follow, and the importance of this document in your Greek journey.

1. Documentation Needed

Before diving into the steps, let's first ensure you have the necessary documents ready:

  • Valid Passport or ID Card

Your primary identification document is essential. Make sure it's up to date, as it will be used for verification purposes.

  • Proof of Address

You'll need to provide proof of your Greek address. This could be a rental agreement, utility bill, furthermore, a certificate of residence from your local municipality.

Pro Tip

If you just landed in Greece and you don’t have an address yet, and you actually need the AFM to rent a house, you can visit KEP  with a local friend or if you are moving for work, someone from the company you may know. Otherwise, you can fulfill a document that this person is hosting in their house. This document has a short validation and can be used to prove your address.

 

  • Residence Permit (if applicable)

Non-EU citizens residing in Greece may require a residence permit. Ensure you have the necessary documents to prove your legal residence status. However, if you are from a country in the EU, you won't need to worry about visa sponsorship or embassy work, you can jump to the next steps.

Also worth reading: 8 hidden Greek islands you must discover

2. Step-by-Step Guide to Obtaining an AFM

Now that you have your documents in order, let's walk through the process of obtaining your AFM:

  • Step 1: Visit the Tax Office

Head to your local Tax Office (known as "ΔΟΥ" in Greek) that serves your area of residence. Furthermore, you can find the nearest Tax Office by consulting local directories or using online resources.

  • Step 2: Request an AFM Application Form

Upon arrival, request an AFM application form, known as "Έντυπο Α.Φ.Μ. 1." You can also download it from the official website of the Independent Authority for Public Revenue (AADE).

  • Step 3: Complete the Application Form

Fill out the application form carefully, providing accurate information about your identity, contact details, and residence.

  • Step 4: Submit the Application

Return the completed form, along with the required documents (passport/ID, proof of address, residence permit if applicable), to the Tax Office.

  • Step 5: Attend an Interview (If Required)

In some cases, the Tax Office may request an interview to verify your details. Therefore, be prepared to answer questions about your financial situation and purpose for obtaining the AFM.

  • Step 6: Receive Your AFM

Once your application is processed and approved, you will be issued an AFM. This unique 9-digit number will be your official tax identification in Greece.

The Importance of the AFM

Now that you have your AFM, you may wonder why it's such a crucial document:

Necessity for Financial Transactions: The AFM is essential for conducting various financial transactions in Greece, including opening a bank account, signing a lease agreement to rent a house, purchasing a car, or investing in local businesses. Moreover, it is a crucial requirement for tax-related matters.

  • Tax Obligations

As a tax identification number, the AFM is linked to your tax obligations in Greece. Consequently, you'll need it to file tax returns, pay taxes, and claim deductions or credits.

  • Business and Employment

If you plan to work or run a business in Greece, you'll need an AFM to comply with local employment and business regulations.

  • Investment

For any investment activities in Greece, whether in real estate or securities, an AFM is typically required to complete transactions.

Conclusion

Obtaining an AFM in Greece is a crucial step for anyone planning to live, work, or invest in this beautiful Mediterranean country. It's more than just a tax number; it's your key to unlocking various opportunities and conducting essential financial transactions. By following the simple steps outlined in this guide and ensuring you have the necessary documentation, you'll be well-prepared to navigate the Greek bureaucracy and enjoy a smooth transition into your new life in Greece. Embrace the culture, the cuisine, and the beautiful landscapes, knowing that your AFM is your trusty companion on this Mediterranean journey.

title: 7 tips to land a job without experience
author: João Penouço
excerpt: In today's competitive job market, landing a job without prior experience is a common challenge. So, how to land a job without experience? There is many ways for you to be hired even if you don't have experience, let's find out!
body:
In today's competitive job market, landing a job without prior experience is a common challenge. However, hiring people with zero experience is a reality that many employers embrace. This article aims to empower candidates to land a job without experience, by highlighting essential qualities and skills that can make them stand out as strong candidates.

Moreover, individuals without experience can demonstrate potential by focusing on punctuality, work ethic, effort, body language, energy, attitude, coachability, and preparedness. These qualities make them valuable assets to organizations. At Atlean World, we promote such roles, and most importantly, we coach our candidates in how to achieve these soft skills that will make you a great fit on your next job interview. Let's find out how you can land a job without experience!

Employers crave punctuality

Punctuality is undoubtedly a critical trait that showcases reliability and respect for others' time. To truly demonstrate your commitment to timeliness and make a lasting impression, consider implementing the following strategies:

  1. Thorough research and planning: Take the time to research the location and plan your route meticulously. Familiarize yourself with potential traffic or unexpected delays. Choose the most efficient way to reach your destination. Having a well-thought-out plan can help you avoid unexpected obstacles and arrive on time.
  2. Arrive early: Aim to arrive at least 10-15 minutes early for meetings, interviews, or any scheduled engagement. Arrive early to show your enthusiasm and preparedness. but also allows you to settle in, compose yourself, and mentally prepare for the upcoming interaction
  3. Familiarize yourself with the company's dress code: Dressing professionally reflects your seriousness and respect for the occasion, leaving a positive impression on those you interact with.
  4. Learn from past experiences: Reflect on any instances where you may have been late in the past, and identify the root causes. Learning from experiences helps you avoid repeating mistakes, even without work experience. Be proactive in recognizing patterns for personal growth.

Work ethic matters

While lacking experience, you can compensate by displaying a strong work ethic and a genuine thirst for learning and growth. There are various ways to compensate and stand out:

  1. Emphasize dedication and timeliness: Highlight your unwavering commitment to completing tasks and meeting deadlines promptly. Even without direct experience, demonstrating a consistent track record of delivering results on time showcases reliability and responsibility.
  2. Express enthusiasm for challenges: Convey your enthusiasm for embracing new challenges and taking on additional responsibilities. Let potential employers know that you are eager to learn and ready to tackle any obstacles that come your way.
  3. Showcase exemplary efforts: Draw attention to instances where you've gone above and beyond the call of duty, such as volunteering or participating in extracurricular activities. These experiences demonstrate your proactive attitude and dedication to personal and professional development.

Demonstrating effort to land the job without experience

Highlighting your ability to put in extra effort can impress potential employers. You can convey the value you bring to the table beyond just the qualifications on your resume. Showcasing commitment to excellence and going above expectations can impress employers, distinguishing you from other candidates, despite no formal experience.

  1. Demonstrate your willingness for additional responsibilities: Illustrate your eagerness to take on extra responsibilities or tasks beyond the scope of your role. Being proactive in expressing your willingness to contribute more showcases your ambition and commitment.
  2. Share examples of personal projects and self-learning initiatives: Share concrete examples of personal projects or self-driven learning endeavors to showcase your proactive approach. Highlighting how you've independently pursued growth can be highly influential.
  3. Express your desire to continuously improve: Demonstrate your genuine desire to continuously improve and grow professionally. Additionally, let employers know that you are receptive to learning from more experienced colleagues, as this portrays humility and a collaborative mindset.
  4. Mention extracurricular involvement: If relevant, discuss any involvement in extracurricular activities or volunteer work that reflects your commitment to making a positive impact in your community or industry.
  5. Share success stories: Furthermore, share success stories from your educational experiences or any other context where you've demonstrated dedication, persistence, and a strong work ethic. These anecdotes will showcase your commitment to achieving goals and overcoming challenges.
  6. Provide references: Whenever possible, offer references who can attest to your go-getter attitude and your ability to go the extra mile in various situations.

Mastering good body language

Non-verbal communication, including body language, plays a crucial role in making a positive impression. It can significantly impact how others perceive you and influence the outcome of various interactions. Mindful body language and positive presentation enhance interpersonal skills, leaving lasting positive impressions on others. A good body language can help you to land a job without experience

  1. Maintain eye contact: Keeping consistent eye contact with others portrays confidence, attentiveness, and active engagement in the conversation or interaction. It signifies that you are genuinely interested in what they have to say.
  2. Practice good posture: Practicing good posture reflects professionalism and attentiveness. Additionally, standing or sitting up straight indicates that you are focused and present in the moment, projecting a sense of reliability and respect.
  3. Use open and welcoming gestures: Using open and welcoming gestures, such as open palms or relaxed arms, conveys approachability and a friendly demeanor. It helps create a comfortable environment for communication and collaboration.
  4. Smiling genuinely: A genuine smile can work wonders in fostering positive connections. It exudes warmth and positivity, making others feel at ease in your presence.
  5. Avoiding fidgeting or nervous habits: Such behaviors can be distracting to others and may convey feelings of anxiety or lack of confidence. Hence, strive to remain composed and attentive throughout the interaction.
  6. Practicing active listening: By nodding and responding appropriately, demonstrating your active engagement in processing the information being shared.

Exuding energy and attitude

By emphasizing your positive energy and attitude throughout the job search process, you showcase your potential as a team player. This will make you a compelling candidate, even if you have no prior experience.

  1. Display enthusiasm and interest: During interviews or networking opportunities, showcase genuine enthusiasm for the role and the company. Let your passion for the industry and the potential contributions you can make shine through.
  2. Emphasize your eagerness to contribute and grow: Effectively communicate your can-do attitude, highlighting your eagerness to contribute to the team and your willingness to take on new responsibilities. Consequently, employers appreciate candidates who approach tasks with a positive and proactive mindset.
  3. Exhibit resilience and adaptability: Emphasize your resilience and adaptability by showcasing instances where you've tackled challenges head-on and learned from any mistakes. As a result, your ability to bounce back from setbacks and grow through experiences can be a strong asset.
  4. Stay positive throughout the process: Consistently maintain a positive demeanor and outlook throughout the job search process, from application submissions to interviews. As a result, potential employers will notice and appreciate your optimistic attitude.
  5. Focus on transferable skills: Even if you lack experience in a particular field, focus on transferable skills and experiences from other areas of your life. Highlight how these skills can be applied to the role you're pursuing.

Being coachable to overcome lack of experience

Employers highly value candidates who actively seek feedback, exhibit a growth mindset, and continuously strive to expand their knowledge and skills. Position yourself as a candidate who actively seeks improvement, welcomes growth opportunities, and is committed to continuous learning. All of which are highly attractive attributes to prospective employers:

  1. Active listening and thoughtful questions: Demonstrate your ability to engage fully with the speaker, discerning not just the words spoken but also the underlying messages and perspectives. By asking insightful questions during discussions, you demonstrate a genuine interest in comprehending and enhancing the conversation.
  2. Express your willingness to accept guidance : Showing openness to change and improvement reflects your receptiveness to new ideas and your dedication to continual professional growth.
  3. Illustrate your ability to integrate real-world feedback: Share personal and academic instances of seeking feedback and applying it for improved outcomes. Emphasize the beneficial results that arose from this iterative learning process.
  4. Continuous learning and self-improvement: This may include participating in workshops, enrolling in online courses, or seeking mentorship opportunities. Additionally, demonstrating enthusiasm for continuous learning showcases dedication to personal and professional development.

Preparation to avoid being caught unprepared

Effective preparation is crucial for overcoming a lack of experience and making a strong impression:

  1. Company research: Thoroughly investigate the company's background, core values, and the specific role you're applying for. Understand the organization's mission and culture for effective alignment and genuine interest in the opportunity.
  2. Interview Readiness: Prepare well-crafted answers to common interview questions, and anticipate potential inquiries regarding your experience gaps. As well as question to ask to the recruiter or employer about the company or the job position. This preparation will help you confidently address any concerns and showcase your potential as a valuable candidate.
  3. Relate achievements: Bring forward pertinent examples from your academic or personal experiences that vividly demonstrate your transferable skills. Demonstrating skills in real-life situations highlights adaptability and potential despite no direct experience.
  4. Relevant internships or apprenticeships: If you have completed internships or apprenticeships, emphasize the experiences and skills gained during these opportunities.

In conclusion

You can land a job without prior experience. It's not only possible but also a viable strategy for organizations seeking individuals with untapped potential. Candidates without experience can excel by embodying punctuality, work ethic, body language, coachability, and preparedness.  Enthusiasm, willingness to learn, and determination make you valuable, even without job-specific experience. Embrace the opportunity, believe in yourself, and showcase the qualities that set you apart from the competition.
